pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Poisoning THE SMOKING GUN: Severe ascending painful neuropathy combined with dramatic alopecia (hair loss) appearing 1 to 2 weeks after initial exposure. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium chemically mimics potassium due to its identical ionic radius. It impairs the sodium-potassium ATPase pump, disrupts cell membrane potential, and interferes with mitochondrial energy production. Additionally, thallium avidly binds to sulfhydryl groups on vital enzymes, selectively destroying tissues with high metabolic turnover, specifically primary sensory axons and hair follicle matrix cells.
